summary: 14-day Nightscout analysis reveals strong overall Time in Range (86.0%), but significant safety risks from Time Below Range (5.1%), peaking overnight (18.5% at 01:00) and in the evening (15.3% at 19:00). High afternoon glucose spikes (up to 293 mg/dL) occur due to 100% reliance on Unannounced Meals (0 logged carbs), triggering aggressive Dynamic ISF SMB microboluses that accumulate high IOB under a 10-hour DIA tail. In addition, max IOB (25.0 U) and max basal (12.0 U/h) limits are excessively wide relative to the total daily dose (~19.7 U/day).

analysis_steps.findings: Telemetry coverage is excellent (98.7% CGM coverage over 14 days, 3,995 valid entries). Profile configuration is fully specified.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 CGM entries, 2,315 treatments, 655 insulin entries (275.95 U total), 0 logged carb entries.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete absence of logged carbohydrate entries (all meals handled via UAM/SMB automation).

analysis_steps.findings: Overall control shows 86.0% TIR, but hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) is 5.1%, exceeding the 4.0% international safety limit. Lows concentrate at 23:00-03:00 local (up to 18.5% TBR) and 19:00 local (15.3% TBR).
analysis_steps.evidence: TBR is 18.5% at 01:00, 15.3% at 19:00, 11.4% at 00:00, and 10.2% at 02:00. Min glucose extreme is 41 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unlogged meals make it difficult to distinguish meal-related late insulin drops from basal-driven hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.findings: The 90 mg/dL nocturnal target (23:00-08:00) offers insufficient safety margin during overnight hours. Daytime basal (0.50-0.80 U/h) is stable, but evening drops at 18:00-19:00 coincide with basal steps up to 0.60-0.70 U/h.
analysis_steps.evidence: Target target_segments: 90 mg/dL 00:00-08:00 & 23:00-00:00; local hourly glucose drops to avg 105.4 mg/dL at 19:00.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Basal testing was not performed; unannounced meal IOB overlaps overnight windows.

analysis_steps.findings: Nominal ISF is 56 mg/dL/U flat, but Dynamic ISF (70%) aggressively reduces effective ISF down to 27.8 mg/dL/U during postprandial highs (>200 mg/dL). DIA of 10.0 hours correctly models modern exponential insulin tails but extends trailing IOB calculation.
analysis_steps.evidence: Profile DIA 10h, ISF 56 mg/dL/U; loop logs report variable_sens ranging from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of logged carbs prevents direct verification of Carb Ratios (10.5-13.2 g/U).

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled and active. Because meals are unannounced, UAM SMBs are the sole meal-dosing mechanism, causing delayed postprandial insulin delivery.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_always_enabled=true; local hourly TAR peaks at 15:00 (32.1% >180 mg/dL).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Meal content and exact timing are unrecorded.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits are critically high relative to insulin needs: max_iob_units is 25.0 U (exceeding total daily dose of ~19.7 U/day) and max_basal_u_per_hour is 12.0 U/h (15x-24x scheduled basal). Dynamic ISF at 70% factor causes aggressive SMB over-dosing during unannounced spikes.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile settings: max_iob_units=25.0, max_basal_u_per_hour=12.0, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=70; total daily insulin avg = 19.7 U/day.

analysis_steps.findings: 0% of meals are pre-bolused or announced. Postprandial spikes reach 200-290 mg/dL at 14:00-17:00, triggering aggressive UAM SMBs that lead directly to 19:00 evening hypoglycemia (15.3% TBR).
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_entries: 0; therapy_response_windows show large post-correction/SMB drops (e.g., 234 to 56 mg/dL).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of logged meals hides true postprandial absorption profile.

analysis_steps.findings: GLP-1 co-therapy (1.25mg notes on Aug 14, 17, 20) slows gastric emptying. Relying on UAM without carb logs or eCarbs creates a mismatch between delayed meal absorption and automated SMB delivery.
analysis_steps.evidence: Representative notes document GLP-1 1.25mg administration; meal_max_absorption_hours=7.0.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No eCarbs or meal entries logged.

analysis_steps.findings: Prioritized action order established: 1. Tighten excessive safety limits (max IOB, max basal) to prevent over-dosing risk. 2. Raise nocturnal target from 90 to 100 mg/dL to curb overnight TBR (up to 18.5%). 3. Moderate Dynamic ISF adjustment factor from 70% to 50%. 4. Encourage prebolusing and carb logging.
analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesis of Checkpoints 1-3 against safety boundaries and decision inventory.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Verification of changes requires 3-5 days of post-implementation monitoring with carb logging.

strengths: High overall Time in Range of 86.0% with a mean glucose of 121.6 mg/dL.
Excellent CGM data completeness (98.7% coverage across 14 days).
Effective automated loop response that prevents prolonged severe hyperglycemia.
issues: Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL) is 5.1%, exceeding the clinical safety threshold of 4.0%, concentrated overnight (23:00-03:00) and evening (19:00).
Safety limits are dangerously excessive: max_iob_units (25.0 U) exceeds 24-hour Total Daily Dose (~19.7 U/day), and max_basal_u_per_hour (12.0 U/h) is 15x-24x baseline basal.
Target glucose of 90 mg/dL overnight provides minimal safety margin against trailing IOB.
100% reliance on Unannounced Meals (0 logged carbs) causes high afternoon spikes (up to 293 mg/dL) followed by Dynamic ISF over-correction and trailing hypoglycemia.
Dynamic ISF adjustment factor (70%) combined with unannounced spikes generates excessive SMB stacking under a 10-hour DIA tail.

recommendations.title: Reduce Max IOB and Max Basal Safety Limits
recommendations.description: Lower max_iob_units from 25.0 U to a conservative limit (e.g. 6.0 U, ~30% of TDD) and max_basal_u_per_hour from 12.0 U/h to 3.0 U/h. This prevents potential dangerous over-dosing from automated SMBs during CGM noise or unannounced meal decay miscalculations.

recommendations.title: Raise Nocturnal Target to 100 mg/dL
recommendations.description: Increase the target glucose from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00. This creates an essential buffer against nocturnal hypoglycemia where TBR currently reaches 10-18.5%.

recommendations.title: Moderate Dynamic ISF Adjustment Factor
recommendations.description: Reduce the Dynamic ISF adjustment factor from 70% to 50%. This softens the aggressive ISF reduction during glucose spikes, preventing excessive SMB microboluses that drive trailing evening hypoglycemia.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise overnight target glucose from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Time Below Range reaches 10.1% to 18.5% between 23:00 and 03:00. Increasing the overnight target to 100 mg/dL provides a necessary safety margin to reduce nocturnal hypoglycemia.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight CGM trends for 3 to 5 nights to verify that TBR drops below 4.0%.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: SMB delivery frequency and duration limits are standard and appropriate.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Current limits (25U max IOB, 12U/h max basal) exceed TDD (~19.7U) and create severe risk during sensor anomalies or aggressive UAM stacking.
Reducing Dynamic ISF adjustment factor from 70% to 50% tempers overly aggressive SMB microboluses during postprandial spikes, reducing trailing hypoglycemia.
Carbohydrate absorption settings are standard and appropriate.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Transition from 100% unannounced meal (UAM) reliance to prebolusing meals 10-15 minutes prior to eating with immediate upfront boluses. This suppresses the steep 14:00-17:00 postprandial spike and prevents Dynamic ISF from over-delivering trailing SMBs.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Current total reliance on UAM causes steep glucose rises that trigger aggressive Dynamic ISF SMB dosing, resulting in high post-meal IOB that drives evening (19:00) and nocturnal (23:00-03:00) hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log carbohydrate amounts and bolus timing for 3-5 consecutive days to observe postprandial peak reduction and verify CR accuracy.

exceptions.pattern: GLP-1 co-therapy or high-fat/protein delayed absorption meals
exceptions.suggestion: Use eCarbs or split boluses (e.g. 50% immediate, 50% eCarbs over 2-3 hours).
exceptions.rationale: GLP-1 delays gastric emptying, making full upfront boluses prone to early hypoglycemia followed by late hyperglycemia.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Reduce max_iob_units from 25.0 U to 6.0 U and max_basal_u_per_hour from 12.0 U/h to 3.0 U/h in AAPS safety settings.
Step 2: Update overnight target glucose from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL for the 23:00-00:00 and 00:00-08:00 segments.
Step 3: Reduce Dynamic ISF adjustment factor from 70% to 50% in AAPS dynamic sensitivity settings.
Step 4: Begin logging carbohydrates and prebolusing meals 10-15 minutes prior to eating.
Step 5: Monitor glucose trends for 3-5 days, focusing on overnight TBR and 19:00 evening stability, before considering further profile changes.
education: Max IOB safety limits should ideally be set relative to your Total Daily Dose (e.g. 20-30% of TDD) to prevent loop algorithms from delivering excessive insulin during unexpected sensor spikes.
Unannounced Meal (UAM) algorithms react only after glucose starts rising, which inherently causes higher postprandial spikes than giving an upfront or pre-meal bolus.
Dynamic ISF increases insulin sensitivity factor when glucose is high; if set too aggressively, it can over-correct spikes and cause hypoglycemia several hours later.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change with their healthcare team.
Make profile and automation adjustments one at a time and monitor glucose closely for several days after each change.
Prioritize safety limit adjustments and hypoglycemia prevention before attempting to optimize meal parameters.
